notes: Every name here was recovered from the registration code of isaac-ng.exe, not from a name table.
Class hierarchy is not included: the binary stores __parent as a table taken from the Lua stack, so the parent name is not recoverable from the registration code.
The three global namespaces (Isaac, Input, Options) are Lua globals, not classes.

The 'argc' and 'returns' fields come from the shape census in tools/probe_body_arity.py: the number of visible arguments the body reads and the number of values it returns to Lua. They are null where the census did not measure the body.

'argc' is an upper bound, not a verified argument count: it is the highest Lua stack index the body (or a helper it calls) touches, so it can exceed the number of arguments the member actually uses. 'argc_evidence' says where the number came from.

A body address is provenance, not identity: the binary reuses one closure body for several members (Vector.X and Vector.Y share 0x008bb2e0, because the field offset travels as an upvalue), so the 'upvalue' field is the part that distinguishes them.
